segmentNote: One business segment: retail of everyday goods. Revenue is 99.96% sale of goods and 0.04% commission from in-store Speedpoint services; China is under 10% (AR p.209, p.216).

revenueFormula.text: Revenue = number of shop visits x average basket

Utilities, repairs, logistics and other costs

metrics.label: Free cash flow after rent FY2025

drivers.evidence: 3,151 outlets at Jun 2026, +257 in a year; target about 250 new outlets a year (AR p.22, Q2 p.11)
drivers.why: The main growth engine: each new shop adds sales. Investors pay a premium while openings stay on track; a slowdown would hurt the valuation.

drivers.evidence: Transactions +13.6% to 146.4m in Q2 2026; basket stable at about RM21 (Q2 p.11)
drivers.why: Growth comes from more visits, not bigger baskets. A falling basket would signal weaker spending.

drivers.evidence: Earlier opening nationwide lifted traffic (Q2 p.11; AR p.22)
drivers.why: Extra sales from existing shops at little extra cost.

drivers.evidence: Added about RM22.4m revenue in 1H2026 (Q2 p.12)
drivers.why: Small today (under 0.5% of revenue); an option for future growth.

drivers.evidence: Management notes softer demand and cautious spending (Q2 p.13)
drivers.why: Essentials are defensive, but weaker spending can slow sales growth per shop.

drivers.evidence: Market is competitive and fragmented: mini-markets, supermarkets, hypermarkets, online grocery (AR p.55, p.46)
drivers.why: Price competition could limit margin gains.

drivers.evidence: Gross margin up from 19.0% (FY2024) to 19.5% (FY2025) and 20.0% (1H2026) from scale and direct sourcing (AR p.44; Q2 p.12)
drivers.why: Every 0.1 percentage point of margin is roughly RM12m of gross profit a year.

drivers.evidence: Personnel costs rose 18.2% to RM862.6m in FY2025, faster than revenue (AR p.211)
drivers.why: The largest operating cost; minimum-wage rises squeeze profit.

drivers.evidence: Utility costs fell in 1H2026 from energy-efficiency upgrades and solar (Q2 p.12)
drivers.why: Offsets part of the wage pressure.

drivers.evidence: Higher depreciation from new shops and warehouses (Q2 p.11-12)
drivers.why: Front-loaded cost of growth; earns back as new shops mature.

drivers.evidence: Opened July 2026, supports about 180 outlets (Q2 p.13)
drivers.why: Removes a bottleneck for opening more shops.

drivers.evidence: 5 pilot outlets in Fuzhou, under 10 more planned (AR p.10; analyst commentary)
drivers.why: Tiny today; success could add a new market, failure costs little.

drivers.evidence: Borrowings fully repaid by Jun 2026; RM884m cash and short-term investments (Q2 p.3)
drivers.why: Lowers financial risk and supports dividends.

drivers.evidence: About 38 times trailing earnings at RM3.03 (see Metrics)
drivers.why: A high multiple prices in steady growth; any earnings miss can hit the share price hard.

outlook: Growth in FY2026 expected from outlet expansion, steady demand for everyday goods, efficiency gains and 99 Bulksales (AR p.46).
New Semenyih distribution centre opened July 2026 to support about 180 outlets (Q2 p.13).
Risks flagged by management: rising wages, utilities and logistics costs; more competition; execution risk while expanding; softer consumer demand (AR p.46; Q2 p.13).
Dividend policy: sustainable returns while keeping enough cash for growth; FY2025 dividends 4.5 sen per share (AR p.46, p.213).
